plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 25% of the book, favoring income and broad index exposure.
Buy LMT for 5% of the book, adding a top-quality name with a strong scanner setup.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation and low drawdown. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, but still carries market risk, especially from its tech exposure.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2%, reducing leveraged ETF exposure while keeping a small allocation.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach and meet the single name mandate.
Buy LMT for 4% of the book, adding a quality name with a strong scanner setup.
Buy NVDA for 3% of the book, adding another quality tech name with a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some tech exposure with reduced leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration, but remains exposed to market fluctuations, particularly in the tech sector.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL, bringing it to 6%, and SPAL to 6%, leaning into leveraged ETFs with strong trends.
Buy LMT for 6% of the book, adding a top-scoring scanner setup.
Buy LUNR for 5% of the book, adding a high R setup from the scanner.
Buy NVDA for 5% of the book, adding another top-scoring scanner setup.
This plan aggressively leans into strong setups and leverage for growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by using leverage and concentrating in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach significantly amplifies both potential gains and drawdowns, with leveraged ETFs experiencing daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the higher risk.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero, eliminating all high-beta leveraged exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 30% of the book, prioritizing income-generating ETFs.
Trim QQQ to 10% to further reduce growth-oriented exposure.
This plan rotates the book towards income and broad index for steady distributions.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield and steady monthly distributions. While prioritizing low drawdown, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff, so it is not a savings account.
